Subject: Redlines: MSA + Order Form (training & output ownership)

Hi Grace / Ben,

Thanks for the call this morning. Attached are BrightTech's proposed redlines to the MSA and Order Form. High-level asks: 

- Customer ownership of model outputs and any derivatives (explicit language in Section 3).
- No use of BrightTech data or outputs to retrain, fine-tune, or improve Redwood models for any purpose without express, paid opt-in (3-year minimum).
- Any feedback or telemetry that could contain customer data must be treated as customer data and not added to any training corpus.

We flagged a few places where the current Redwood feedback license and telemetry language could be read as allowing general model training; that is a hard stop for us. We appreciate Redwood's position on iterative product improvements, but we need a clear carveout for BrightTech's proprietary content.

Please let us know if Redwood can agree to the draft language or if you'd prefer a short legal-to-legal call this week. My colleague Priya (cc'd) is our outside counsel and will handle redline negotiation.

Attachments: BrightTech_MSA_redlines_20261101.docx, BrightTech_OrderForm_v2_redline.pdf

Best,
Maya Singh
Director, Strategic Programs

Ben / Grace — thanks for the quick replies. We are primarily focused on two clauses: (1) Output ownership (we will not accept a license that implicitly grants Redwood rights to outputs or derivatives); and (2) Training exclusion (we need an explicit prohibition on using BrightTech Data or Customer Outputs to train any Redwood model, for a minimum of three (3) years from the Effective Date, unless BrightTech provides express, written consent).

We circulated the attached revised redline that clarifies the model-training prohibition and provides sample wording for "Customer Data" and "Customer Outputs." Please review and indicate where Redwood would propose alternate wording.

From: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com; ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: legal@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-03T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: suggested counter-positions for BrightTech redlines

Karthik / Ben — after a quick review with Legal and Product, here's a pragmatic counter we should be comfortable proposing on Thursday:

1) Output ownership — Accept customer ownership of direct outputs generated by prompts tied to BrightTech Content. Add a defined exception: Redwood retains the right to productize system-level improvements that are not attributable to BrightTech outputs (e.g., fixes for model stability, latency). Proposed language: "Customer retains ownership of Customer Outputs. Redwood may not claim ownership of Customer Outputs, but may use aggregated, non-attributable signals for product improvement."

2) Training exclusion — Offer a 3-year opt-out by default (i.e., Redwood will not use Customer Data or Customer Outputs for model training unless Customer provides written consent). However, keep an explicit carve-in for de-identified, aggregated telemetry used strictly for operational metrics and safety monitoring, with a narrow definition of "de-identified" and audit rights for BrightTech. This preserves BrightTech's control while allowing Redwood to maintain product health.

3) Feedback license — Convert the broad feedback license to a two-tier structure: (A) Customer-proprietary data and outputs: opt-out by default (no use for training); (B) non-proprietary anonymized feedback: standard feedback license applies.

4) Ops & Evidence — we'll attach an operational note describing telemetry scrubbing, retention windows, and audit logs (Ben to produce). Offer a 90-day delivery timeline for any additional contractual paperwork once the high-level language is agreed.

I'm attaching an internal suggested redline (RW_internal_suggested_redline_BrightTech_20261103.docx) with clause excerpts. If this approach sounds good, Ben can send the call invite to Priya / Maya for Thursday 10am PT and Karthik can prepare two short clause options.

Thanks,
Grace
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@brighttech.com>; Priya Shah <priya.shah@brighttech-legal.com>; grace.oconnor@redwood.com; ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-04T17:45:00-08:00
Subject: Revised clause excerpts for BrightTech — proposal ahead of Thursday call

Hi Maya / Priya — per our internal review, attaching two short clause excerpts we believe bridge the parties' needs. Below are the key excerpts (redline-ready):

1) Customer Outputs: "Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to Customer Outputs. Except as expressly authorized in this Agreement, Redwood shall not use Customer Outputs for any purpose other than to provide the Services to Customer. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may use aggregated, non-attributable telemetry and metrics for product reliability and safety; such telemetry shall not include Customer Outputs or Customer Data in identifiable or re-creatable form."

2) Training and Model Use: "Redwood shall not, and shall ensure its affiliates and subprocessors do not, use Customer Data or Customer Outputs to train, fine-tune, or improve any foundation models or model weights, for a period of three (3) years from the Effective Date, unless Customer provides written, separate consent specifying scope and compensation. The parties agree that operational metrics that are de-identified and aggregated do not constitute \"use\" for training purposes."

3) Audit & Verification: "Upon reasonable notice and during regular business hours, Customer may request an audit limited to Redwood's telemetry scrubbing processes and attestations that Customer Data was not used for model training in violation of this clause. Redwood shall cooperate and provide redacted evidence where appropriate to protect Redwood's proprietary systems."

We can drop these into the redline and walk through them on Thursday. Ben will send the calendar invite; the DocuSign placeholder will be ready once the commercial sheet is agreed.

Thanks for working through this — we think the two-tier feedback + narrow operational exception is commercially fair and preserves product safety.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product Legal Partnerships, Redwood Inference
